label: digit 2 input at original position 5 or later
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the digit 2 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 5 (orig_idx 5-8). It does not fire on 2 at positions 0-4, on any other token, on <DEL>, or anywhere in the copy phase (including copied 2s). Magnitude rises with position: t=5 activations are lowest (about 0.25-0.3 of max), t=6 around 0.55-0.6, and t=7-8 highest (0.8-1.0); per-step mass shares match this (t=8 holds 10% of activations but 17% of mass). Dev precision and recall are both 1.0.

issues: None found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0 and mass recall 1.0 (n_active = n_predicted = 27578). The misses command finds 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Profile (dev split) supports every factual claim. All activation is in the original phase, with 0 on the delimiter and 0 in the copy phase. The feature fires only on in_tok '2', and only at t=5-8 (orig_idx 5-8), at a constant rate of about 0.033-0.034 per orig_idx. It is 0 at t=0-4.

The magnitude claims match mean activation per step worked out from mass share x total mass / count. In units of max (2.986): t=5 about 0.28, t=6 about 0.59, t=7 about 0.79, t=8 about 0.89. The claim that t=8 has about 10% of activations but 17% of mass is confirmed (2789/27694 actives, 0.167 of mass).

Minor caveat: the per-t means are computed estimates. The rising magnitude shows up as a correlation of 0.92 rather than 1.0, which fits a binary predicate and is not a gap. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
